title: COMPARISON
notes:
✓ Comparison → comparing two or more people, things, places, actions, or qualities.

◆ THREE DEGREES OF COMPARISON
✓ Positive → basic form: tall.
✓ Comparative → compares two: taller.
✓ Superlative → compares three or more: tallest.

✓ Positive → Addis Ababa is a large city.
✓ Comparative → Addis Ababa is larger than Dire Dawa.
✓ Superlative → Addis Ababa is one of the largest cities in Ethiopia.

title: DEGREES OF COMPARISON
notes:
✓ Positive degree → describes a quality without comparing.
✓ The car is fast.

✓ Comparative degree → compares two things or people.
✓ The car is faster than the bus.

✓ Superlative degree → shows the highest or lowest degree among three or more.
✓ The car is the fastest in the race.

✓ Comparative → usually + than.
✓ Superlative → usually the + adjective + -est or the most + adjective.

title: SHORT ADJECTIVES
notes:
✓ Most one-syllable adjectives form the comparative with -er and the superlative with -est.

✓ tall → taller → tallest
✓ small → smaller → smallest
✓ fast → faster → fastest
✓ cheap → cheaper → cheapest
✓ young → younger → youngest

◆ PATTERN
Adjective + -er / -est.

✓ My brother is taller than me.
✓ He is the tallest student in the class.

title: SPELLING RULES
notes:
✓ Adjectives ending in -e → add -r/-st.
✓ large → larger → largest
✓ nice → nicer → nicest

✓ Consonant + y → change y to i.
✓ happy → happier → happiest
✓ easy → easier → easiest

✓ One-syllable adjective ending consonant-vowel-consonant → double the final consonant.
✓ big → bigger → biggest
✓ hot → hotter → hottest
✓ thin → thinner → thinnest

✓ Do not double letters unnecessarily.
✓ fast → faster, not fastter.

title: LONG ADJECTIVES
notes:
✓ Most adjectives with two or more syllables use more and most.

✓ beautiful → more beautiful → most beautiful
✓ expensive → more expensive → most expensive
✓ important → more important → most important
✓ comfortable → more comfortable → most comfortable

✓ This book is more interesting than that one.
✓ She is the most intelligent student in the class.

✓ Avoid double comparison.
❌ more better
❌ most fastest
✓ better
✓ fastest

title: TWO-SYLLABLE ADJECTIVES
notes:
✓ Some two-syllable adjectives can take either -er/-est or more/most, while others normally use more/most.

✓ happy → happier → happiest
✓ narrow → narrower → narrowest
✓ simple → simpler → simplest
✓ careful → more careful → most careful

✓ When uncertain with a longer adjective, more/most is generally safer.

title: IRREGULAR COMPARISON
notes:
✓ Some adjectives have irregular forms:

✓ good → better → best
✓ bad → worse → worst
✓ far → farther/further → farthest/furthest
✓ little → less → least
✓ much → more → most
✓ many → more → most

✓ This book is better than that one.
✓ She is the best student in the class.
✓ Today is worse than yesterday.
✓ He has the least money.

✓ These forms must be learned individually.

title: COMPARATIVE + THAN
notes:
✓ Use than after a comparative when comparing two things or people.

✓ John is taller than David.
✓ This exercise is more difficult than the previous one.
✓ My car is faster than yours.

✓ Pronouns after than can be formal or informal depending on the structure.
✓ She is taller than I am. → formal/complete.
✓ She is taller than me. → very common in everyday English.

◆ KEY STRUCTURE
Comparative + than.

title: SUPERLATIVE + THE
notes:
✓ Superlatives normally use the before the adjective.

✓ He is the tallest student.
✓ This is the most expensive car.
✓ She is the best player.

✓ Do not normally omit the when the adjective directly modifies a noun.
❌ He is tallest student.
✓ He is the tallest student.

✓ A possessive can sometimes replace the.
✓ This is my best friend.
✓ That was her greatest achievement.

title: EQUAL COMPARISON
notes:
✓ Use as + adjective + as to show that two things are equal in a quality.

✓ John is as tall as Peter.
✓ This car is as expensive as that one.

✓ Negative comparison → not as/so + adjective + as.
✓ John is not as tall as Peter.
= Peter is taller than John.

✓ This book isn't as interesting as that one.

✓ as...as → equality.
✓ not as...as → inequality.

title: NOT AS...AS
notes:
✓ Not as...as means that the first person or thing has a lower degree of the quality.

✓ A is not as tall as B.
→ B is taller than A.

✓ This phone is not as expensive as that phone.
→ That phone is more expensive.

◆ TRANSFORMATION
A is not as fast as B.
= B is faster than A.

A is not as good as B.
= B is better than A.

title: COMPARATIVE STRUCTURES
notes:
✓ Comparative + than
→ This road is longer than that road.

✓ much/far/a lot + comparative
→ This road is much longer.
→ She is far more experienced.

✓ slightly/a little/a bit + comparative
→ This bag is slightly cheaper.

✓ even + comparative
→ The situation is even worse.

✓ Comparative and comparative
→ The weather is getting colder and colder.

✓ These structures strengthen or weaken the degree of comparison.

title: THE...THE COMPARATIVE
notes:
✓ The + comparative..., the + comparative... expresses a linked change.

✓ The more you study, the more you learn.
✓ The harder you work, the more successful you become.
✓ The higher we go, the colder it gets.

◆ PATTERN
The + comparative + clause, the + comparative + clause.

✓ Meaning → one change causes or corresponds to another change.

title: DOUBLE COMPARATIVES
notes:
✓ Repeated comparative adjectives can describe a continuing increase or decrease.

✓ The weather is getting colder and colder.
✓ The population is becoming larger and larger.
✓ Technology is becoming more and more advanced.
✓ Life is getting more and more expensive.

✓ Short adjective → comparative + and + comparative.
✓ Long adjective → more and more + adjective.

title: SUPERLATIVE WITH IN / OF
notes:
✓ Use of when comparing members of a group or set.
✓ She is the tallest of the three sisters.

✓ Use in when referring to a place, organization, period, or group.
✓ He is the fastest runner in the school.
✓ This is the best restaurant in the city.

✓ of + group/set.
✓ in + place/organization/context.

title: COMPARING TWO VS THREE OR MORE
notes:
✓ Comparative → normally used to compare two.
✓ Which is bigger, A or B?

✓ Superlative → normally used for three or more.
✓ Which is the biggest of the three?

✓ In modern English, comparative forms can sometimes be used in larger sets when considering alternatives or making pairwise comparisons, but school grammar generally teaches:

◆ 2 → comparative.
◆ 3+ → superlative.

title: COMPARISON WITH NOUNS
notes:
✓ Compare quantities using more, less, fewer, as many, and as much.

✓ more + countable/uncountable noun
→ I have more books.
→ I need more water.

✓ fewer + countable plural noun
→ She has fewer books than me.

✓ less + uncountable noun
→ He drinks less water.

✓ as many + plural countable noun + as
→ I have as many books as you.

✓ as much + uncountable noun + as
→ She has as much money as he does.

title: FEWER VS LESS
notes:
✓ Fewer → normally used with countable plural nouns.
✓ fewer students
✓ fewer cars
✓ fewer mistakes

✓ Less → normally used with uncountable nouns.
✓ less water
✓ less money
✓ less time

✓ There are fewer students today.
✓ We have less time today.

✓ Countable → fewer.
✓ Uncountable → less.

title: MORE / MOST WITH NOUNS
notes:
✓ More → greater quantity.
✓ I need more information.
✓ She has more books than I do.

✓ Most → greatest quantity or the majority, depending on context.
✓ He has the most books in the class.
✓ Most students passed the exam. → majority, not superlative comparison.

✓ Most does not always mean 'the greatest' in the same grammatical sense.

title: COMPARISON WITH ADVERBS
notes:
✓ Adverbs can also have comparative and superlative forms.

✓ fast → faster → fastest
✓ hard → harder → hardest
✓ carefully → more carefully → most carefully
✓ efficiently → more efficiently → most efficiently

✓ She runs faster than me.
✓ He works more carefully than his brother.
✓ She works the most efficiently in the team.

✓ Short adverbs often use -er/-est; longer adverbs commonly use more/most.

title: COMMON ERRORS
notes:
❌ more better
✓ better

❌ most fastest
✓ fastest

❌ more easier
✓ easier

❌ He is tallest than me.
✓ He is taller than me.

❌ He is taller as me.
✓ He is taller than me.

❌ She is as taller as me.
✓ She is as tall as me.

❌ He is the most tall student.
✓ He is the tallest student.

❌ There are less students here.
✓ There are fewer students here.

❌ This is the best of the city.
✓ This is the best in the city.

✓ Avoid using two comparison markers for the same adjective.

title: SENTENCE TRANSFORMATION
notes:
✓ Comparative transformations:

✓ John is taller than Peter.
= Peter is shorter than John.

✓ This book is more expensive than that one.
= That book is less expensive than this one.

◆ EQUALITY TRANSFORMATION
✓ John is taller than Peter.
= Peter is not as tall as John.

◆ SUPERLATIVE TRANSFORMATION
✓ No other student in the class is taller than John.
= John is the tallest student in the class.

✓ These transformations are common in grammar examinations.

title: COMPARISON WITH 'ONE OF THE'
notes:
✓ One of the + superlative + plural noun → identifies one member among the highest group.

✓ She is one of the best students in the class.
✓ Addis Ababa is one of the largest cities in Ethiopia.

✓ The noun after 'one of the' must normally be plural.
❌ one of the best student
✓ one of the best students

title: LIKE / AS IN COMPARISON
notes:
✓ Like → preposition; commonly followed by a noun/pronoun.
✓ He runs like his father.

✓ As → conjunction/preposition depending on structure; can introduce a clause.
✓ He works as his father does.

✓ She looks like her mother.
✓ She works as her mother does.

✓ Like → similarity.
✓ As → often introduces a role or clause showing manner/comparison.

title: PREFER / WOULD RATHER
notes:
✓ Prefer → expresses one choice as more desirable than another.

✓ I prefer tea to coffee.
✓ She prefers walking to driving.

✓ Would rather + V1 → preference in a particular situation.
✓ I would rather stay home.
✓ I would rather walk than take a taxi.

◆ PATTERNS
Prefer + noun + to + noun.
Prefer + V-ing + to + V-ing.
Would rather + V1 + than + V1.

title: COMPARISON MASTER GUIDE
notes:
◆ 1. Two things → comparative + than.
✓ A is bigger than B.

◆ 2. Three or more → the + superlative.
✓ A is the biggest of the three.

◆ 3. Equal → as + adjective + as.
✓ A is as big as B.

◆ 4. Unequal → not as/so + adjective + as.
✓ A is not as big as B.

◆ 5. Increasing change → comparative + and + comparative.
✓ It is getting colder and colder.

◆ 6. Linked change → the + comparative..., the + comparative...
✓ The more you study, the more you learn.

◆ 7. Quantity → more/fewer/less.
✓ more books, fewer books, less water.

◆ 8. Stronger comparison → much/far/a lot + comparative.
✓ much better.

◆ 9. Weaker comparison → slightly/a little + comparative.
✓ slightly cheaper.

◆ 10. Group ranking → one of the + superlative + plural noun.
✓ one of the best students.

✓ Golden rule → Never use two comparison forms together: ❌ more better, ❌ most fastest, ❌ more easier.
